label: WRONG
reason: The only outlier, electron-builder.config.cjs, is the app's packaging config and by design consumes packaging/buddy/release helpers (targets, signing, native-host resources), which are the release tooling for this very app (package.json scripts also drive them); it is build tooling, not app code, so 0 of 1 counted outliers is a mistake and a new builder/release config would be flagged wrongly. label: WRONG
reason: Not TRIVIAL: restricted-imports.mjs has no scripts/ ban and eslint.config.mjs only ignores scripts/** itself. The sole outlier apps/admin/next.config.ts is build-time config, not app source. It deliberately imports the shared bootstrap helpers (load-workspace-env, resolve-monorepo-root, sentry/next-config, copy-maplibre-worker-assets) the same way apps/donor and apps/missionary next.config.ts do. It is neither the definition nor an aggregator, so it counts as legit (R1), and 0 of 1 counted outliers makes the rule WRONG mixed_group. App source members (payload.config.ts, proxy.ts, published-content-reader.ts) import nothing from scripts. Hesitated with ACCEPT, because runtime app code importing scripts/ would be a real layering slip.
